newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 9.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- President Jiang Zemin met United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan, saying China's will not practise hegemonism or seek territorial expansion.
- A high-speed passenger train linking Beijing with Kowloon will go into service from May, ending the absence of direct trains between the Chinese capital and Hong Kong.
- Premier Li Peng wrote a letter to a national meeting on correcting malpractices in various industries, calling for improvement in party discipline.
- Output of the Baoshan Iron and Steel Group will reach 11 million tonnes after the completion of the plant's third phase.
- Shanghai Meishan (Group) Co Ltd will issue 200 million yuan in bonds from May 15 to June 13.
- China will invest 100 billion yuan a year in its telecommunications industry to the year 2000.
- China's industrial output from January to April was worth 625.0 billion yuan, up 11.4 percent compared with the same period of 1996.
- A survey by the Ministry of Forestry shows 17.6 percent of China's territory is desert.
- Xinjiang's gold industry saw its output increase by 20.84 percent in 1996, realising a profit of more than 75 million yuan.
- The National People's Congress debated sustainable development, the ecology and environment, improving northwest China and protecting fluorite resources.
- Premier Li Peng urged the world community to help African nations tackle their economic problems.
- Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang condemned Sao Tome and Principe for establishing diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
